item.title: AQL in Practice: Sampling, Defect Classes and Reading the Report
item.description: AQL 2.5 does not mean 2.5% defects allowed. How the sampling tables actually work for toy orders, what critical/major/minor should cover, and how to act on a report instead of just filing it.

item.title: Payment Terms with Chinese Toy Factories: T/T, L/C, and When to Walk Away
item.description: 30/70 T/T is standard, but the details decide who carries the risk. How payment terms work with Chinese toy factories, the red flags of bank-fraud scams, and when to refuse.

item.title: Plush Toy Sourcing Guide: Fabric, Filling and Fire Safety
item.description: A plush toy is only as good as its fabric weight, filling and stitching. How to write a spec sheet Chinese factories can quote from, the five QC checks that catch bad batches, and where EN71-2 fire testing actually bites.

item.title: Small Batch Toy Sourcing: 100–500 pcs Without Getting Ignored
item.description: Factories quote 1,000 pcs minimum because small orders are unprofitable for them, not because they dislike you. Five ways to get 100–500 pcs at a workable price, plus the real premium to expect.

item.title: Toy Landed Cost: The 9 Costs Buyers Forget
item.description: FOB price is not your cost. A worked example of nine landed-cost items for a toy container — freight, duty, VAT, port fees, inspection and FBA — and how to calculate them.

item.title: Pet Toy Export to the US: What Actually Applies
item.description: Pet toys are not covered by CPSIA, which surprises most buyers. Here is what does apply — FDA feed rules for edible chews, state chemical laws, Amazon documentation, and labeling.

item.title: Why Custom Plush Toy Quotes Differ by 3x
item.description: Three factories quote USD 2.40, USD 4.10 and USD 6.80 for the same plush design. Here is what is actually different in each quote, and how to compare them line by line.

item.title: How to Lower MOQ with Chinese Toy Factories (Without Paying More)
item.description: Why Chinese toy factories set minimum order quantities, which levers actually move them, and the four tactics that get a 1,000-piece MOQ down to 300 without a price penalty.

item.title: How to Verify a Chinese Toy Factory Before You Pay a Deposit
item.description: Nine checks that separate a real toy manufacturer from a trading company, what each document proves, and the two questions that get a straight answer on a factory video call.

item.title: Yiwu Sourcing Agent vs Alibaba vs Buying Direct: Which Wins in 2026?
item.description: A line-by-line comparison of sourcing toys via a Yiwu agent, Alibaba, or direct from a Chinese factory: real cost, hidden risks, and fit by order size.

item.title: Yiwu Toy Sourcing Guide 2026: How to Find Reliable Manufacturers in China
item.description: A comprehensive guide to sourcing toys from Yiwu in 2026. Learn where to find reliable factories, how to negotiate MOQs, and avoid common pitfalls.
